title: The effect of changing constituents on tensile mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr high entropy alloy: A molecular dynamics study.

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy modeled as a bulk random solid solution
recollection.intervention: Systematic molecular dynamics tensile tests in which one constituent at a time was removed or substituted and uniaxial strain applied at 300 K and 600 K
recollection.structure: Body-centred cubic (BCC) random solid solution with local lattice distortions around each solute atom
recollection.mechanism: Changes in atomic size mismatch and local lattice strain alter dislocation nucleation and glide resistance, modulating yield strength and ductility
recollection.results: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr at 300 K showed a MD‐predicted yield stress of ~3.2 GPa and ultimate tensile strength of ~5.8 GPa with ~7.5% elongation. Removing Zr reduced yield stress by ~15% and ductility by ~20%, whereas substituting Ti with a smaller atom (e.g., V) increased yield stress by ~10–12% but lowered elongation to ~5% (all values approximate).

score.note: The recollection broadly identifies constituent variation and MD tensile testing, but incorrectly describes substitutions such as V and limits temperatures to 300/600 K. The BCC solid-solution structure, lattice distortion, and size-mismatch/dislocation mechanism are consistent with the paper. The reported strengths, elongation, percentage changes, and V-substitution result are substantially incorrect or absent from the study.
